rca.rootCause: In DateTime._bind_to_schema (and likely similar methods in Date/Time/DateDelta), the code accesses `schema.opts` directly to resolve the format. When a DateTime field is used as an inner field of a container field (List/Tuple/Mapping), the container field calls `self.inner._bind_to_schema(field_name, self)`, passing the container field object as the `schema` argument. Since Field objects do not have an `opts` attribute, this raises AttributeError. The fix is to use `self.root.opts` instead of `schema.opts`, which correctly resolves to the actual Schema object at the top of the field hierarchy.
evidence: The traceback shows the error occurs at `fields.py` line 1117: `or getattr(schema.opts, self.SCHEMA_OPTS_VAR_NAME)` with `AttributeError: 'List' object has no attribute 'opts'`
The traceback shows List._bind_to_schema at line 636 calls `self.inner._bind_to_schema(field_name, self)`, passing the List field itself as the schema parameter to the inner DateTime field
The hints confirm the fix: change `getattr(schema.opts, self.SCHEMA_OPTS_VAR_NAME)` to `getattr(self.root.opts, self.SCHEMA_OPTS_VAR_NAME)` to correctly access the root Schema's opts
The test file includes a regression test `test_datetime_list_inner_format` that verifies DateTime fields inside List and Tuple containers respect the format set in the Schema's Meta class
